## Frontend Defaults

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-roles.sh from each rule's strength line. Change the rule, then rebuild; do not edit this file. -->

Each line is one rule: its title, its one sentence, and the file that holds it.

- **Inject collaborators instead of passing an options bag.** A composable gets its runtime collaborators by injecting their ports (the typed capabilities a root provides); its arguments are only identity and real per-instance configuration. [`frontend/inject-collaborators-instead-of-passing-an-options-bag.md`]
- **Pass local dependencies as props and events.** A dependency between one component and its child is a prop and an event, not a port (a typed capability provided to a whole subtree). [`frontend/pass-local-dependencies-as-props-and-events.md`]
- **Keep composition roots free of business logic.** A composition root (the app shell, a layout, or a page) creates implementation composables, provides ports, and composes components; it holds no business logic and no inline pure transforms. [`frontend/keep-composition-roots-free-of-business-logic.md`]
- **Do not hide composition in global setup.** Do not put composition (creating implementation composables and providing ports) in the app shell, which is set up once for every page, unless the capability is genuinely app-wide. [`frontend/do-not-hide-composition-in-global-setup.md`]
- **Keep logic free of framework imports.** Files in `logic/` are pure TypeScript: no imports from `vue`, `nuxt`, `#imports`, or any framework package. [`frontend/keep-logic-free-of-framework-imports.md`]
- **Put pure functions in logic.** Anything that can be a pure function lives in `logic/`: transforms, immutable data shaping, mapping a server value to a label, colour, icon, or order, and checks on client state with their limits taken from the DTO. [`frontend/put-pure-functions-in-logic.md`]
- **Keep a port file to its type and pair.** A port file holds only the port's type and its `[injectX, provideX]` pair from the `useProvideInject` helper; it imports types and that helper, never `provide`, `inject`, or a value from `vue`, and declares nothing else. [`frontend/keep-a-port-file-to-its-type-and-pair.md`]
- **Shape a port around operations, not DTOs.** Give each feature concern one port (a type that names a capability the UI needs), shaped around the operations the UI needs from that boundary, not one port per function, per DTO, or per generated client. [`frontend/shape-a-port-around-operations-not-dtos.md`]
- **Expose refs only from a provided context.** A capability port exposes plain values and functions; only a provided context, the reactive view-model made for a Vue subtree, exposes `Ref` or `ComputedRef`, and it is not presented as framework-neutral. [`frontend/expose-refs-only-from-a-provided-context.md`]
- **Create port pairs with the typed helper.** Create every port's `[injectX, provideX]` pair with the one `useProvideInject` helper: its inject throws when called outside a provider, and its provide returns the exact implementation it was given, not the narrowed port type. [`frontend/create-port-pairs-with-the-typed-helper.md`]
- **Inject the port, not its implementation.** A component or composable that depends on a provided capability imports `injectX` from `ports/`, not the implementation composable or the adapter (the implementation of a port). [`frontend/inject-the-port-not-its-implementation.md`]
- **Keep adapters free of Vue and presentation state.** An adapter (the implementation of a port) translates between a port and HTTP, a generated client, storage, or a platform API; it holds no presentation state, and a pure adapter imports nothing from Vue or Nuxt. [`frontend/keep-adapters-free-of-vue-and-presentation-state.md`]
- **Let a stateful composable implement the port.** When an implementation is already reactive and stateful, the composable returns the port-shaped capability and the root provides it directly; add a pure adapter only when there is pure logic worth separating. [`frontend/let-a-stateful-composable-implement-the-port.md`]
- **Check an implementation with satisfies.** Check that a composable's result meets its port with `implementation satisfies Port`, not a `(): Port` return annotation, when it has members only the composition root needs. [`frontend/check-an-implementation-with-satisfies.md`]
- **Give a composable one capability.** A composable may hold reactive state, client calls, side effects, and local UI orchestration, and it returns a surface for one capability (something the code needs done for it) rather than growing to cover several. [`frontend/give-a-composable-one-capability.md`]
- **Keep components presentational.** A component renders data, holds local UI interaction, emits events, and may inject an already-provided capability; it never calls a generated client, runs a workflow, constructs infrastructure, or reaches round its composition root (the app shell, a layout, or a page). [`frontend/keep-components-presentational.md`]
- **Call the generated client in the implementing composable.** Call the generated client (the typed API client generated from the transport contract) inside the composable or adapter that implements the capability, not in a component. [`frontend/call-the-generated-client-in-the-implementing-composable.md`]
- **Colocate page code with its page.** Code used by one page lives in that page's folder, under `components/`, `composables/`, `logic/`, `ports/`, and `adapters/`. [`frontend/colocate-page-code-with-its-page.md`]
- **Never import another page's local code.** A page or layout subtree never imports from another page's local folders (`components/`, `composables/`, `logic/`, `ports/`, `adapters/`). [`frontend/never-import-another-pages-local-code.md`]
- **Promote shared code to a feature or shared.** When more than one subtree needs a product capability, its port and pure logic move to `app/features/<feature>/` (a feature is a product capability several pages or layouts use), and code no feature owns moves to `app/shared/`; an implementation only one root constructs stays beside that root, and one several roots construct may live in the feature. [`frontend/promote-shared-code-to-a-feature-or-shared.md`]
- **Import a feature only through its index.** Consumers import a feature (a product capability several pages or layouts use) only through its public entry point, `app/features/<feature>/index.ts`, never its internal files. [`frontend/import-a-feature-only-through-its-index.md`]
- **Keep page state out of global stores.** Do not use a global store as the default home for state, or to carry unrelated concerns between components; state that one page or layout owns lives in a composable at that root. [`frontend/keep-page-state-out-of-global-stores.md`]
- **Call useState only inside a composable.** Nuxt `useState(` appears only inside `composables/` files; the composable owns the key, and every other layer (components, pages, plugins, logic, adapters) calls the composable, never the string key. [`frontend/call-usestate-only-inside-a-composable.md`]
- **Build frontends as single-page apps.** Build a frontend as a single-page app and do not use server-rendering idioms. [`frontend/build-frontends-as-single-page-apps.md`]
- **State the user's job before designing controls.** Before designing controls, state who is doing this, the outcome they want, the decisions they must make, which of those depend on earlier ones, and what they must see to trust the result, then turn those answers into the page structure. [`ui/state-the-users-job-before-designing-controls.md`]
- **Make the headings read as the user's journey.** A setup flow's headings alone, read top to bottom, tell the user's journey in their terms, not the implementation's. [`ui/make-the-headings-read-as-the-users-journey.md`]
- **Ask for outcomes, not mechanisms.** A control asks a question the user can answer from what they know about their own work, not one about the mechanism behind it. [`ui/ask-for-outcomes-not-mechanisms.md`]
- **Collapse technical variants into one user action.** When several technical variants implement one user intention, offer the intention as one action and let the editor it reveals cover the variants. [`ui/collapse-technical-variants-into-one-user-action.md`]
- **Order by the user journey.** Order decisions as the user reasons about the task (establish context, make the primary choice, configure only what it requires, handle exceptional behaviour, review the result, confirm or save), and never ask a later question before the user has the context for it. [`ui/order-by-the-user-journey.md`]
- **Keep dependent controls beside their choice.** Keep a dependent control next to the choice that reveals it. [`ui/keep-dependent-controls-beside-their-choice.md`]
- **Group one decision at a time.** Each visual section answers one user question; do not group controls because their values share a backend object, and do not split one decision across cards because separate operations or models implement it. [`ui/group-one-decision-at-a-time.md`]
- **Present the same decision the same way everywhere.** Present a decision that is the same in concept with the same control, wording, and order wherever it appears. [`ui/present-the-same-decision-the-same-way-everywhere.md`]
- **Make the default legible.** A selected default says what it will do, and where its consequences are not obvious, says why it suits. [`ui/make-the-default-legible.md`]
- **Make every default safe.** Offer a recommended default where the product has a safe, common choice, and never a default that silently overwrites data, widens access, or loses information. [`ui/make-every-default-safe.md`]
- **Prefer progressive disclosure.** Make the common path understandable at once, and show an advanced option only when it is selected or needed, never showing every technical mode at once, empty advanced editors by default, or uncommon complexity competing with the recommended path; this presents information where it becomes relevant, it does not hide what is necessary. [`ui/prefer-progressive-disclosure.md`]
- **Hide a choice that has only one option.** A dropdown whose only option is the default it already holds is hidden but kept mounted until a second option exists, with the default's outcome stated as text in its place where that is not obvious. [`ui/hide-a-choice-that-has-only-one-option.md`]
- **Pick a required choice that has one candidate.** A required choice with one candidate is picked for the user. [`ui/pick-a-required-choice-that-has-one-candidate.md`]
- **Keep a target picker visible with one candidate.** A target picker (which stage, which list, which column) stays visible even with one candidate, and so does a lone stale "(unavailable)" option. [`ui/keep-a-target-picker-visible-with-one-candidate.md`]
- **Use domain language.** Use the words users meet in their work rather than words from the implementation, unless the intended user genuinely uses the technical word, and introduce an unavoidable technical term through familiar language. [`ui/use-domain-language.md`]
- **Explain consequences, not system events.** A label says what will happen to the user's work, not what the system does internally. [`ui/explain-consequences-not-system-events.md`]
- **Use help text for the user's next question.** Supporting text explains a material consequence or answers the user's likely next question; it never restates the label. [`ui/use-help-text-for-the-users-next-question.md`]
- **Show the result.** Where the user would otherwise have to run the rules in their head, show the resulting outcome: the final file path, generated filename, recipient summary, permission effect, schedule, filter result, or mapped data. [`ui/show-the-result.md`]
- **Keep a preview live and marked as an example.** A preview updates as the configuration changes, uses representative sample values, and is clearly marked as an example, not a live operation. [`ui/keep-a-preview-live-and-marked-as-an-example.md`]
- **Make the final summary match what will happen.** The final review or summary states exactly what will happen when the user confirms. [`ui/make-the-final-summary-match-what-will-happen.md`]
- **Treat disabled states as explanations.** A disabled control shows why it is disabled and how to enable it: hide an irrelevant control until its prerequisite is chosen, show the prerequisite beside it, or say in plain words what the user must do. [`ui/treat-disabled-states-as-explanations.md`]
- **Describe the action, not the step number.** Guidance names the action the user must take; a step number is only a secondary aid, since numbering changes and users think in tasks. [`ui/describe-the-action-not-the-step-number.md`]
- **Follow the GOV.UK Design System for open details.** Where the spec or design leaves accessibility, formatting, display, or validation open, find the matching component or pattern in the GOV.UK Design System and style guide, follow it, and name it in the spec or in your summary of the work. [`ui/follow-the-govuk-design-system-for-open-details.md`]
